claims: Coal is a combustible black sedimentary rock.
Coal is primarily used as a fossil fuel to generate electricity and produce steel.
Coal supplies about a quarter of the world's energy.
Coal is formed over millions of years from compressed, decayed plant matter in swamps.
Anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, and lignite.
Coal is extracted via surface or underground mining.
Coal originates from prehistoric vegetation (trees, ferns) in wetlands.
Prehistoric vegetation in wetlands died and was buried under layers of dirt and rock 300 million years ago.
Over millions of years, heat and pressure (known as coalification) compressed organic matter.
Coalification turns organic matter first into peat, then into coal.
Coal acts as a store of energy originally captured from the sun.
Coal is ranked based on its carbon, moisture, and heat content.
Anthracite is the highest rank of coal.
Anthracite is the hardest coal.
Anthracite has the most carbon.
Anthracite has a shiny, metallic luster.
Bituminous coal is a middle-rank coal.
Bituminous coal is soft black coal.
Bituminous coal is used for generating electricity.
Bituminous coal is used for making coke for steel.
Subbituminous coal is black and dull.
Subbituminous coal has low-to-moderate heating values.
Subbituminous coal is used for power generation.
Lignite is the lowest grade of coal.
Lignite is brown coal.
Lignite has high moisture.
Lignite has lower carbon content.
Lignite is primarily used for power.
Coal-fired power plants burn coal to heat water into high-pressure steam.
High-pressure steam drives turbines to produce electricity.
Metallurgical (coking) coal is essential for reducing iron ore to iron in steel manufacturing.
Coal is used in cement production.
Coal is used in paper manufacturing.
Coal is sometimes used for heating.
Coal is found in seams within layered sedimentary rock formations worldwide.
Major coal deposits exist in the U.S., Russia, China, and India.
Surface mining (strip mining) is used when coal is near the surface.
Surface mining involves removing surface soil and rock (overburden).
Underground mining is used for deeper coal deposits.
Underground mining requires shafts and tunnels for miners to extract coal.
Coal mining destroys landscapes.
Coal mining disrupts ecosystems.
Burning coal releases carbon dioxide (CO2).
Burning coal releases sulfur dioxide (SO2).
Burning coal releases heavy metals.
